title: Bean Delivery
opening: A sack of beans has arrived at the door. Dadu never trusted a sack he had not tested.

intro.p: A farmer has come all the way to the workshop with a sack of cacao beans on his shoulder.

talk: Assalamu alaikum, apa. I used to bring your grandfather his beans every year.
Wa alaikum assalam. I am Laila. I am sorry, he is not here anymore.
I know. I am sorry. His sack is still his sack, though. Will you take it?
I do not know yet. How do I tell good beans from bad ones?
Cut them open and look inside. Your grandfather had a card for it.
Then I will check every bean, and smell the sacks, before I pay.

lines.text: {blank} the pods to get the wet beans out.
{blank} the beans in heaps for days, so the flavour builds.
{blank} the beans in the sun, on mats.
Cut a handful open and look inside. [[torn:…good beans are brown, with open cracks…]]
Smell the first two sacks. [[q:A good sack smells of mild vinegar and fruit.]]
Smell the next two. Smoke and sharp ammonia are both bad signs.

clues.title: Kobir's note
clues.text: "After the pods are cut, the beans sit in heaps to ferment. Then we dry them in the sun. Last, we bag them."

clues.title: Dadu's cut-test card
clues.text: Five beans cut in half, drawn by Dadu. A good bean is brown inside with open cracks. Purple means not fermented long enough. Grey and hard means not fermented at all. Mouldy or flat means it is empty or spoiled.

clues.title: Dadu's smell card
clues.text: "Good: mild vinegar and fruit. Bad: smoky, because the beans were dried over a fire. Bad: ammonia, a sharp sting, because they were left to ferment too long."

clues.title: The old scale
clues.text: Dadu weighed every sack twice. "Weigh it, don't guess," he said.

clues.title: Kobir's gamchha
clues.text: A checked cotton towel, left on the hook last year. Kobir always wiped his forehead with it.

steps.title: How beans are made
steps.prompt: Tap a farm step, then tap its blank in the notebook. Or drag it there.
steps.say: The page is stained again. Kobir's note should tell me the order on the farm.

machines.name: Bag
machines.does: packs the dry beans into sacks
machines.says: Bagging. It comes last, once the beans are dry.

machines.name: Dry
machines.does: spreads the beans out in the sun
machines.says: Drying in the sun. It keeps the beans from going mouldy.

machines.name: Cut
machines.says: Cutting the pods. It comes first.

machines.name: Ferment
machines.does: piles the beans up for days
machines.says: Fermenting. The beans sit in heaps for days, and the flavour builds.

lets the flavour build, over days

steps.title: Line 2: the cut test
steps.prompt: Each bean is cut in half. Tap the bad ones before they slide off the tray. Tap a bean to stop it. Missed beans come round again.
steps.say: Brown with open cracks is good. Dadu's card shows the rest.

types.label: Purple inside
types.why: Purple means it was not fermented long enough. It will taste sharp and bitter.

types.label: Grey and hard
types.why: Grey and hard, like slate, means it was never fermented. It will taste of nothing.

types.label: Mouldy
types.why: Mould would spoil the whole batch.

types.label: Flat and empty
types.why: Flat beans have no nib inside. There is nothing to use.

params.goodTap: That one is good. Keep it.
params.stillBad: Some bad beans are still on the tray. They will come round again.
params.staticNote: With reduced motion on, the beans stay in a grid. Tap the bad ones.

feedback.correct: Five bad beans out. The rest are brown and cracked, just as Dadu's card says.

hints: Dadu's cut-test card in the Workshop shows what a good bean looks like.
Keep only the brown beans with open cracks. Take out the purple, the grey and hard, the mouldy and the flat ones.

steps.title: Line 3: smell the sacks
steps.prompt: Smell both sacks. Which one is good?
steps.say: Two sacks. Dadu's smell card says what a good sack smells like.

options.label: Sack A
options.sense: A mild sour smell, like vinegar, with something fruity under it.

options.label: Sack B
options.no: That smoke means the beans were dried over a fire. The smell will end up in the chocolate.

params.idleSense: Tap a sack to smell it.

feedback.correct: Mild vinegar and fruit. That is how a good sack smells.

hints: Dadu's smell card says what a good sack smells like. Look in the Workshop.
A good sack smells of mild vinegar and fruit, so it is Sack A.

steps.title: Line 4: one more pair
steps.prompt: Two more sacks. Smell them both and pick the good one.
steps.say: Again. Smoke is bad, and so is a sharp sting.

options.label: Sack C
options.sense: A sharp sting in your nose, like cleaning fluid.
options.no: That sting is ammonia. The beans were left to ferment too long, and they have gone bad.

options.label: Sack D
options.sense: A mild sour smell, like vinegar, with something fruity under it.

params.idleSense: Tap a sack to smell it.

feedback.correct: Sack D. Kobir keeps his beans well.

hints: Dadu's smell card also says what the bad smells mean. Check it in the Workshop.
Take the sack that smells of mild vinegar and fruit, which is Sack D.

talk: "Your grandfather would have said the same: good beans make good chocolate."
I will buy your beans every year, Kobir Bhai.
Then I will bring the best sack first, apa.
recipe: Cut the pods, ferment in heaps, dry in the sun, bag the beans
Cut a handful open: keep the brown, cracked beans
Take out purple, grey and hard, mouldy and flat beans
A good sack smells of mild vinegar and fruit, not smoke or ammonia
reveal.realFact: In real life, the flavour of chocolate is set long before the workshop, by how the beans are fermented and dried on the farm.
